title: HYBRID: grade to rank, compare only where grades are close: does routing between the two formats beat either? (zero calls)
question: Both formats already judged the same 1,971 matches, so every routing rule is a re-read of the caches; pointwise verdict when the grade gap exceeds tau, pairwise otherwise; tau swept 0 to 100; tau* = smallest pairwise budget reaching accuracy >= 0.864 AND 0 top-4 violations; prediction tau* ~ 10-20, 25-40% budget, ~half the calls.

criteria.text: smallest pairwise budget reaching accuracy >= 0.864 AND 0 top-4 violations
criteria.value: accuracy peaks 0.883 at tau = 30, above BOTH parents (pairwise 0.864, pointwise 0.808); no tau reaches 0 top-4 violations (the inversion returns as soon as any pairwise verdict enters, because close-grade pairs ARE the frontier pairs); cost 1.86 + 2 x budget with a floor of 36% budget (that many pairs have exactly equal grades), never cheaper than either parent

predictions.value: no tau meets the clauses; floor 36% budget

plain_description.what: Using cached verdicts from both judging formats on the same 1,971 matches, it uses the grade-only verdict when two answers' grades are far apart and the head-to-head comparison when they are close. It sweeps the threshold. No calls.
plain_description.why: It tests whether mixing the two formats gives better accuracy at lower cost than either one.
plain_description.information: Success would give a cheaper, more accurate judging recipe. Result: failed on two of three requirements. Accuracy peaks at 0.883, above both formats. But no setting fixes the order of the top models, because close-grade pairs are exactly the top pairs, and the mix is never cheaper. Advice: rank with grades only, and use the mix only for individual verdicts. Later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
